title: Cozze alla Marinara
subtitle: Mussels in tomato, garlic, and white wine
excerpt: Cozze alla marinara are mussels cooked in a sauce of tomato, garlic, white wine, and olive oil. The mussels open in the sauce and release their briny juice into it, which enriches the tomato base. Serve with bread to mop up the cooking liquid, which is the best part.
sourceNotes: Cozze alla marinara is a Neapolitan and southern Italian classic, one of the most widely made mussel preparations in Italy. It is closely related to the French moules mariniere and shares its core technique, though the Italian version is more likely to include tomato. Mussels are farmed along the Adriatic and Tyrrhenian coasts and are consumed in large quantities in Puglia, Campania, and Liguria.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Clean the mussels up to 1 hour ahead and keep in cold water. Cook and serve immediately; mussels do not reheat well.

content.text: Cozze alla marinara are mussels cooked in a tomato and white wine sauce. The mussels open in the hot liquid and release their salt water into the sauce, which deepens its flavour. The whole dish takes under 20 minutes and produces a deeply flavoured pot with more sauce than mussels, which is correct: the bread to mop it up is as important as the mussels themselves. Discard any mussels that do not open.

items.prepNote: scrubbed, beards removed, any open ones discarded

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot with a lid over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes if using. Cook for 2 minutes until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the white wine and let it bubble for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce has reduced slightly.
Tip in the mussels and put the lid on. Cook over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally, until all the mussels have opened. Discard any that remain closed.
Scatter the parsley over the top. Serve immediately in deep bowls with plenty of bread.

Mussels in tomato sauce are common along every Italian coast, but the Neapolitan and Puglian versions are best known. Taranto in Puglia is the centre of Italian mussel farming and has a strong mussel-cooking tradition. A note on the name: the marinara sauce here is not the same as the pizza marinara. The mussels and their brine make it a different dish from the pizza topping.
